requirements.requirement: On node1, /srv/data is kept recoverable through filesystem snapshots (a working snapshot mechanism is in place with a baseline snapshot captured)
requirements.summary: No LVM/spare block device existed on the base XFS root, so the executor created a loop-backed LVM PV/VG/LV, mounted it at /srv/data, populated application data, and took an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap) as the recoverable baseline. Snapshot creation and listing/checksums are directly observed.
config.txt changed, records.db deleted, two junk files added post-snapshot; before/after listings and content directly show the modification.

requirements.requirement: Restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: lvconvert --merge performed against lv_data_snap, volume remounted, and a full sha256 diff against the pre-modification baseline reported CONTENT_MATCHES_BASELINE_EXACTLY; config.txt content confirmed reverted to the original version.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (dfdea52d...) and healthy mount/LVM/data state were captured, systemctl reboot was issued with an acknowledgement, the connection dropped/timed out during the reboot window, and a new boot_id (80dd7a45...) was observed afterward — matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity cross-check. Post-restart verification directly shows srvdata.service active/enabled, LVM VG/LV active, /srv/data mounted, and data checksums still matching the original baseline, demonstrating the full pre-disruption/disruption/recovery transition.

overall_summary: The executor built a working LVM-based snapshot mechanism for /srv/data (necessary since no spare device existed), captured a baseline snapshot, modified the directory, and restored the exact pre-modification content, verified by an exhaustive sha256 diff — fully satisfying the public task contract. It additionally ran the independent node-restart evidence protocol competently: pre-restart health capture, reboot acknowledgement, a genuinely changed boot identity consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart recovery of the mount, LVM state, systemd unit, and data integrity. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified beyond a few small residual temp files.
limitations: The public task contract does not itself require restart/persistence, so the restart-protocol evidence is treated as supplemental and does not by itself raise or lower the core task score, only confidence in overall system robustness.
Minor /tmp residue (log and checksum files) was not cleaned up, though this is low-risk and does not affect functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task: LVM install and loop-backed PV/VG/LV/mount creation were necessary prerequisites (no spare block device existed on the base XFS root, confirmed by the initial discovery command), snapshot creation/modification/restore directly satisfy the core outcome, and the systemd persistence unit plus fstab cleanup (cmd-39a11cbc3b234da0) was a reasonable, low-risk mutation supporting the boot-persistence needed for the restart-evidence protocol (fstab replaced by a more robust boot-time script rather than left broken). No unnecessary or unreverted experimental mutations were found; no failed services or unsafe exposure appeared in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare. Minor residue: a handful of small log/checksum files were left under /tmp (lvm_install.log, pre_restart.sha256, post_restart.sha256, restored.sha256, reboot.log), which is bounded and low-risk but was not cleaned up.
